jobs.title: Alum and instructor Willie Castro achieves prestigious GM World Class Technician status
jobs.description: Cerritos College alum and instructor Willie Castro achieves prestigious GM World Class Technician status Printer-friendly version FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: May 27, 2026 Media Contact: Aya Aoki; Public Relations and Communications NORWALK, Calif. – May 27, 2026 – Cerritos College’s Automotive Mechanical Repair Instructor Willie Castro has earned the prestigious General Motors World Class Technician status. This esteemed recognition represents the highest level of excellence a GM technician can attain. The journey to becoming a World Class Technician is rigorous and demanding. Technicians must meet strict certification requirements through training programs offered by the GM Service Technical College and the National Institute for Automotive Service Excellence (ASE). The World Class Technician program allows technicians to validate their extensive knowledge and showcase their skills across various automotive service areas, earning them the title of “one and only GM expert.” Willie, a proud alumnus of the Cerritos College Automotive Mechanical Repair Program, has taught part-time at Cerritos College for over 20 years and has over 37 years of experience in the automotive industry. He also serves as a Field Service Engineer for General Motors and is an ASE Advanced Level Specialist with master certifications in Automotive and Medium/Heavy Truck Technician. His background includes work at GM and as a Master Diagnostic Technician for Audi, where he developed expertise in advanced diagnostics and electrical systems. At Cerritos College, he teaches in the GM ASEP Program, covering basic and advanced automotive systems, as well as electric vehicle (EV) systems and safety. "Congratulations to Willie for achieving General Motors World Class Technician status. Only about 7-8 percent of GM technicians reach this level, as the process is quite rigorous. In the United States, there are over 40,000 technicians, yet fewer than 3,000 have attained this honor. Willie is truly dedicated to preparing the next generation of automotive professionals with the essential skills needed for a technology-driven industry,” said Joe Mulleary, professor and chair of the Automotive Mechanical Repair program at Cerritos College. Cerritos College’s GM ASEP program has been a driving force in California’s workforce development since 1979, becoming a national model for equity-driven workforce transformation. Students benefit from advanced classroom instruction and participate in paid internships at local GM dealerships, where they gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge automotive technologies and build professional networks for high-demand jobs. The program was named a 2025 Examples of Excelencia award winner and a finalist in the 2026 Bellwether Awards. About Cerritos College: Cerritos College serves as a comprehensive community college for southeastern Los Angeles County. Communities within the college’s district include Artesia, Bellflower, Cerritos, Downey, Hawaiian Gardens, La Mirada, Norwalk, and portions of Bell Gardens, Lakewood, Long Beach, Santa Fe Springs and South Gate. Cerritos College offers nearly 300 degrees and certificates in nine divisions. Annually, more than 5,000 students successfully complete their course of studies, and enrollment currently averages 21,000 students. Visit Cerritos College online at www.cerritos.edu. -END-

jobs.description: Assistant Professor in Structural Geology and Geomechanics Stanford University University Tenure Line Opening at: Jun 8 2026 - 2:30pm PDT View favorites The Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences at Stanford University and the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability invite applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in the geology and mechanics of rocks and deformation of the Earth's crust. We seek candidates whose research addresses how rocks deform, fracture, flow, and interact with fluids in the upper crust, using field observation as a foundation and quantitative methods, including experimental, numerical, or analytical, to understand the underlying processes. The department has longstanding strengths in structural geology, geomechanics, and tectonics, and seeks to hire in these areas broadly defined. We welcome applications from candidates working in regional tectonic and structural analysis, structural petrology and metamorphic systems, fault zone mechanics and rock deformation, reservoir and subsurface geomechanics, experimental rock physics and deformation, coupled thermos-hydro-mechanical systems, and the mechanics of magmatic-hydrothermal and mineral resources. Candidates working at the intersection of these traditions, for example, connecting regional structural geology to subsurface fluid systems, or applying geomechanical methods to active tectonic problems, are encouraged to apply. As a unit within the Doerr School of Sustainability, the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences is interested in candidates whose research connects to societally relevant problems, including but not limited to earthquake hazards, subsurface energy systems such as geothermal energy and geological carbon storage, critical minerals, and the mechanical integrity of engineered subsurface systems. We also welcome candidates in more fundamental aspects of structural geology and crustal deformation whose work contributes to these areas through basic scientific insight. Candidates conducting field-based studies and capable of teaching field geology are of interest. The successful candidate will teach courses in structural geology, tectonics, or related areas at undergraduate and graduate levels, advise students, and participate actively in the department and school communities. jobs.description: Public Relations Public Relations Home Campus Calendars Campus Connection Frequently Used Forms Press Releases Siskiyous Style Guide (contact Public Relations) Staff Web Content Year-End Reviews Foundation Eagle's Nest Resale Shop Foundation College of the Siskiyous Paramedic Program Instructor Theresa Gowan Honored with Statewide Clinical Excellence Award For Immediate Release: May 21, 2026 Public Relations Office Dawnie Slabaugh Phone: (530) 938-5373 Email: slabaugh@siskiyous.edu Weed / COS – College of the Siskiyous is proud to announce that Theresa Gowan, Lead Faculty of the College of the Siskiyous / Mendocino College Satellite Paramedic Program Training Center has been selected as a recipient of the prestigious Clinical Excellence Award from the California Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Authority as part of this year's statewide EMS Awards program Selected from a highly competitive pool of more than 175 nominations submitted from across California, this recognition highlights Gowan's exceptional clinical skill, dedication, and unwavering commitment to patient care in the emergency medical services profession. "The dedication and commitment demonstrated through this nomination exemplify the highest standards of clinical care in the EMS profession," said Ashley Williams, Deputy Director of Legislative and External Affairs in an email announcement. "We are honored to recognize individuals whose work reflects such excellence and impact in patient care." The Clinical Excellence Award recognizes EMS professionals who consistently demonstrate superior clinical performance, critical thinking, and compassionate care in high-pressure environments. Theresa Gowan's selection reflects not only individual achievement but also the strength and professionalism of the broader EMS community. Gowan was formally notified of the award in March, with an official award presentation by Kirk Thomsen – Paramedic Program Director & EMS Coordinator and Dr. Jeremiah Sims – Dean of Career & Technical Education on April 3. "We are incredibly proud of Theresa Gowan for receiving this well-deserved statewide recognition. Her selection from such a competitive field of nominees across California is a testament to the high caliber of instruction and clinical expertise she brings to our Paramedic Program," said Dr. Char Perlas, Superintendent/President. "At College of the Siskiyous, we strive for excellence in our Career and Technical Education programs, and Theresa embodies the dedication, skill, and compassion we hope to instill in all our students. This award not only honors her individual mastery of the profession but also highlights the strength of the partnership between Siskiyous and Mendocino College in preparing the next generation of EMS first responders." About the EMS Awards Program The California EMS Awards program recognizes outstanding individuals and organizations that exemplify excellence, leadership, and innovation in emergency medical services. Honorees are selected based on their impact, professionalism, and dedication to advancing quality patient care throughout the state. About the College of the Siskiyous EMS/Paramedic Program The Paramedic Program trains students to provide immediate care to the critically ill and injured. Paramedics determine the nature and extent of illness or injury, provide advanced life support, communicate with emergency medical services personnel and transport patients to the hospital. The paramedic program is a highly interactive, fast paced, hands-on experience, requiring student participation. This program meets or exceeds all state and national guidelines for paramedic training, and includes Anatomy and Physiology, Advanced Cardiac Life Support, Pediatric Advanced Life Support, Pediatric Education for Pre-hospital Providers, Advanced Medical Life Support, International Trauma Life Support, and Geriatric Emergency Medical Services. Students who successfully complete the requirements for this program will be prepared for the Paramedic National Registry examination. The curriculum may also academically prepare the student to transfer to a four-year university to complete a Baccalaureate degree program. Learn more about the Paramedic program at College of the Siskiyous or send an email to cteinfo@siskiyous.edu.

Documentary Directed by Sacramento State Professor Kathy Kasic Wins Emmy FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEMay 29, 2026 MEDIA CONTACTS: Becky Repka, Director of Marketing and Strategic Communications (becky.repka@csus.edu)Carol Nicknig, Marketing Specialist (carol.nicknig@csus.edu) University Communications; California State University, Sacramento Documentary Directed by Sacramento State Professor Kathy Kasic Wins Emmy® Award The Memory of Darkness, Light, and Ice honored with a News & Documentary Emmy® Award for Outstanding Science and Technology Documentary SACRAMENTO, Calif., May 29, 2026 — The Memory of Darkness, Light, and Ice, directed by Sacramento State associate professor and filmmaker Kathy Kasic, has won the News & Documentary Emmy® Award for Outstanding Science and Technology Documentary, presented May 28 in New York City. Produced by Metamorph Films and funded by the National Science Foundation, the documentary received the Emmy® Award in a competitive category that included productions from NOVA, National Geographic Documentary Films, and Netflix. The production was an international collaboration involving 17 academic and scientific institutions and 10 student filmmakers, including seven Sacramento State students. The award recognizes the film's innovative blend of climate science, history, and storytelling. The Memory of Darkness, Light, and Ice investigates evidence that Greenland's ice sheet collapsed in the past and examines what that history may reveal about the planet's future. The film centers on a remarkable scientific discovery: sediment recovered from beneath the Greenland Ice Sheet that reveals a previously ice-free Greenland and provides critical insights into climate change. “It was a tremendous honor to be among so many great documentary filmmakers last night. This award elevates not just the film, but also the voices of the scientists and the documentary’s funder, the National Science Foundation,” said Kathy Kasic, director of the film, principal of Metamorph Films and associate professor in Sacramento State's Department of Communication Studies. “As a scientist and filmmaker, my work aims to unify scientific research and share it with the public. This is especially important when the science we urgently need to hear is being attacked.” The documentary traces the story of Camp Century, a secret U.S. Army facility constructed beneath the Greenland Ice Sheet during the Cold War. While the military installation was intended to support plans for deploying nuclear missiles, scientists working at the site drilled through nearly a mile of ice and recovered sediment from beneath the ice sheet. Forgotten for decades, the sediment later yielded groundbreaking evidence about Greenland's environmental past. Since its release, the film has received widespread acclaim, earning the Best Environmental Filmmaking Award at the Wild & Scenic Film Festival and the Best Feature Documentary Award at the Raw Science Film Festival in New York City. It has screened at major scientific, educational, and policy venues, including the American Association for the Advancement of Science, the U.S. Capitol, Columbia University, NYU Tisch School of the Arts, the University of Vermont, and institutions across Europe and Latin America. “The Emmy Award is a remarkable achievement that reflects Kathy's extraordinary scholarship, creativity, and commitment to climate science,” said Jenny Stark, chair of Sacramento State's Department of Communication Studies. “Professor Kasic shows how faculty can involve students in real-world experiences that make a difference internationally. We are very proud of Kathy, our students, and everyone who helped share this important story with audiences everywhere.” The project was supported primarily through a National Science Foundation grant, Collaborative Research: A Fossil Ecosystem Under the Ice: Deciphering the Glacial and Vegetation History of Northwest Greenland Using Long-Lost Camp Century Basal Sediment, with additional support from the European Research Council, California State University, Sacramento, Metamorph Films, and other partners. The film has U.S. and Canadian distribution through Gravitas Ventures and is available on Amazon Prime Video, iTunes, Fandango, YouTube, Vimeo, and cable television platforms. Internationally, it is distributed by ARTE and has been translated into French, Spanish, German, and three Greenlandic dialects.
